# Sync people from the CRM into Google Groups

## Context

Group membership is maintained by hand. `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts:12` hardcodes a
2025 spreadsheet id and six `camp|class|group` mappings that must be edited every season.
`gam/scripts/update-groups-from-roles:30-45` hardcodes the same group list again for volunteer
roles. Groups are both mailing lists and security groups — the portal gate reads one
(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate-bootstrap.ts:18`) — so stale membership is an
access problem, not only a comms problem. This work is carved out of #71.

Two things block a sync:

1. **`programs` is a Clubspot Camp, not a program.** `schema.yaml:224-248` and
   `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts:10-14` model one row per camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. "2026
   Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are separate rows, so
   nothing durable can carry a group.
2. **The sync's bookkeeping does not generalize.** `sync_runs` / `sync_program_runs`
   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/sync-log.ts:22-71`) and `campBackoff`
   (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/backoff.ts:39-72`) are one job's run log, not a queue. A failed camp
   is retried on its own cadence with no per-item retry, no visible backlog, and no way for a second
   job to reuse any of it.

## Approach

Five schema changes, one shared queue, one new Cloud Run job.

### Schema (`packages/crm/schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/`)

**`programs` splits into `programs` + `offerings`.** `offerings` takes `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`,
`start_date`/`end_date`, and a nullable `program_id`. `programs` keeps `name` and gains `group_id`.
`sessions`, `classes`, `registrations`, and `custom_field_definitions` repoint their `program_id` FK
to `offering_id`. Breaking: no manual Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs.

Clubspot has no durable program id, so **staff link an offering to its program by hand**, once per
offering. `planPrograms` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/schedule.ts:88-94`) becomes `planOfferings` and
never writes `program_id`, so the link survives a re-sync. Staff already touch each new offering to
set its class groups, so this adds no new habit. An offering with no program is an audit finding.

**`groups`** — one row per Google Group: `email`, `name`, `settings_template`, `parent_id` self-FK.
`programs.group_id` points at the program group. `classes.group_id` points at the class group and is
set per offering. Non-program groups (`all@`, `staff@`) live here too, replacing the GAM "Group
Templates" worksheet (`gam/scripts/apply-templates:8`).

**`program_roles`** — `person_id`, `program_id`, `role` (`parent_coordinator`, `group_manager`),
nullable `starts_on`/`ends_on`. Separate from `event_staff` (`schema.yaml:140-166`): `event_staff` is
person-plus-session and Clubspot-derived, this is person-plus-program and hand-entered. Mixing
sync-owned and hand-entered rows in one collection is exactly the trap #137 describes.

**`audit_findings`** — `kind` (`unexpected_member`, `settings_drift`, `missing_group`,
`unlinked_offering`), `group_email`, `detail`, `status` (`open`, `dismissed`). Staff dismiss a row and
the dismissal persists across runs. No Google Sheet, so `groups-sync` needs no Sheets dependency.
Possible home for a review UI later (#133).

**`sync_tasks`** — the durable queue: `queue`, `kind`, `key`, `parent_id` self-FK, `status`,
`attempts`, `max_attempts`, `run_after`, `last_error`, `started_at`, `finished_at`. `key` is the
target's natural key, so a re-enqueue updates a pending task instead of piling up. A task may enqueue
children, which makes a run a readable tree in the Directus UI.

### The queue lives in `packages/crm`

`DirectusClient` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/directus.ts:58`) moves to `packages/crm/src/client.ts`,
and the queue planner and worker loop join it. `crm` already exports the row types for anything
reading the CRM, `sync_tasks` is a CRM collection, and `crm` has no dependencies to invert — both
syncs already depend on it or will. `crm` gains one dependency, `winston`. No new package.

The worker is a thin executor over `DirectusClient`; the decisions (which task is claimable, next
`run_after`, when to fail permanently) are pure functions with unit tests, following the
`clubspot-sync` convention.

### `clubspot-sync` moves onto the queue

`sync_runs` and `sync_program_runs` become `sync_tasks` rows: one `run` parent, one `offering` child
each. `SyncLog` (`sync-log.ts:57-73`) is deleted.

`backoff.ts` does **not** collapse into `run_after` — verify this before rewriting it. `run_after`
covers retry after failure. `campBackoff` answers a different question: this offering has changed
nothing for N runs, so poll it less often. That is durable per-offering state, and so is the
watermark (`watermarkForCamp`, `sync-log.ts:12-18`), which today is reconstructed from run history
that the queue will prune. Both move to columns on `offerings`: `synced_through` (timestamp) and
`quiet_runs` (integer). The backoff decision stays a pure function; its input becomes one row instead
of the whole run log, which is simpler than today.

### `gsuite` gains a Directory client

`packages/gsuite/src/directory.ts`: `DirectoryClient` (groups, members) and `GroupSettingsClient`,
both taking an `Auth.GoogleAuth` like `CalendarClient` (`packages/gsuite/src/calendar.ts:26`) and
wrapping every call in `safeCall` (`packages/gsuite/src/common.ts:85`). Impersonation is the caller's
problem, not the client's.

### `packages/groups-sync` (new Cloud Run job)

Depends on `commodore`, `crm`, `gsuite`. No `clubspot-sdk`, no Parse. Pure plan functions, thin
executor, on the `clubspot-sync` pattern.

**Membership of a class group**, add-only, never remove:

- Participants with a `registration_entries` row of status `confirmed`
  (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/registrations.ts:38-74`) for a session of that class.
- Their guardians: `contacts.person_id` where `related_person_id` is the participant and
  `relationship_type` is `guardian` (`packages/crm/src/people.ts:18-27`). Never emergency contacts.
- The participant's own email is always included when set, which is what makes an adult with no
  guardian row work without a special case.
- Dedupe by lowercased, trimmed email, so a family sharing one address is added once.

The Directory API accepts an external address as a member. The group must have
`allowExternalMembers: true`, which the participants template already sets
(`gam/templates/participants.json:2`).

**Settings and nesting**: apply the `groups.settings_template` JSON through the Groups Settings API,
and make each class group a member of its program group (`groups.parent_id`).

> Nesting does not resolve for cross-domain members. `hasMember` follows nested groups in-domain
> only, and `checkTransitiveMembership` needs Enterprise or Cloud Identity Premium, which CSC does
> not have. A program group must not be used as an oauth2-proxy allowlist (#65, #98) until that is
> solved elsewhere.

**Managers and owners**: managers come from `program_roles` rows that are current on the run date.
Owners come from a config list of the break-glass super-admins — `master@` today, `commander@` once
#81 lands.

**Audit**: one pass per run compares live membership and settings against the plan and writes
`audit_findings` rows for the differences. It never removes anyone.

### Auth and infrastructure

The job runs as a new `groups-sync-runner` service account
(`packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap/groups-sync.ts`, mirroring `bootstrap/clubspot-sync.ts:6`).
Writing groups needs `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.group` and
`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.groups.settings` — both wider than the read-only scope the
substrate holds today (`docs/manual-setup.md:99-101`), so this is a separate identity, not a reuse of
`substrate-runner`.

Two ways to get those scopes:

1. **Domain-wide delegation**, impersonating a Workspace admin. This is the repo's only proven path.
   It needs the service account to hold `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on itself, exactly as
   `packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/substrate.ts:33-37` does for oauth2-proxy, plus a new
   manual step in `docs/manual-setup.md` §5.
2. **A Workspace admin role assigned directly to the service account**, which would avoid
   impersonation entirely. I could not confirm from this repo whether Workspace supports this for the
   Directory and Groups Settings APIs. Try it first in the Admin console. Fall back to delegation.

Either way the credential is ADC, no key file, and the job stays compatible with #83's move to
per-task impersonation: the scopes and the impersonated subject are `main.ts` arguments.

Directus access is a second static token with its own machine user, following
`clubspot-sync-directus-token` (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus.ts:62`). Its
policy is read on `people`, `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `classes`,
`offerings`, `programs`, `groups`, `program_roles`, and write on `sync_tasks` and `audit_findings`
only. No GCP project roles. Nothing changes in `config.ts` — this identity is not a deployer.

### What can be tested

Every plan function is pure and unit tested. The Directory and Groups Settings clients are tested
against a mocked `googleapis` boundary, as `packages/gsuite/test/calendar.test.ts` does. Two things
can only be checked live: that the delegation grant works, and that Google accepts a settings
template as written. Check both with a `--dry-run` run against one throwaway group before the first
real run, and keep `gam/scripts/export-groups` and `export-group-members` as the read-back.

## Alternatives

- **Directus Flows for the workflow.** An event router, not a workflow engine: no persisted execution
  state, no resume after a restart, no retry, and Run Script is isolated-vm with no network, so it
  cannot reach Google at all.
- **Cloud Tasks, GCP Workflows, or Temporal.** Temporal's datastore costs more than the substrate VM
  beside it. Workflows' YAML steps are not unit testable, which fights the plan-function convention.
  Neither is needed at this scale, and the driver is failure visibility, not latency.
- **A durable class entity above the offering.** Four levels before a person, still needs a
  per-offering mapping step, and no home for `all@`.
- **A `google_group_email` string on the class row.** No home for settings or nesting.
- **Naming the new level `season`, `term`, or `edition`.** `season` is one letter from `sessions`.
  `term` reads as a shared calendar period. `edition` reads wrong for a recurring class.
- **A new package for the queue.** `sync_tasks` is a CRM collection and `crm` already exports its row
  types. A package whose only job is to wrap one collection is not worth the build tier.

## Open questions

1. **Linking an offering to its program by hand.** The design assumes staff pick the program on each
   new offering, roughly a dozen times a year. The alternative is a `program_matchers` rule table
   matching camp names by pattern, which is more code and silently mislinks on a renamed camp.
   Confirm the manual link is acceptable.
2. **Assigning a Workspace admin role directly to the service account.** Unconfirmed. If it works,
   the delegation step in `docs/manual-setup.md` is unnecessary. Decide after trying it.
3. **Sync notifications (#122).** The queue makes failures visible in Directus, which weakens the
   case for a Chat message. Still out of scope here, and still one answer for both syncs.
4. **Assumptions to correct if wrong.** A program gets a group only if `group_id` is set — there is no
   other rule. The #71 boundary is unchanged: Groups for discussion, Listmonk later for the
   newsletter, both reading the CRM. Group owners come from a config list, not from the CRM.

## Steps

1. **Split `programs` into `programs` + `offerings`.** `schema.yaml`, `packages/crm/src/schedule.ts`,
   and the `clubspot-sync` rename (`schedule.ts`, `registrations.ts`, `sync-run.ts`, tests) in one
   commit — the build breaks if they are separated.
2. **Add the `groups`, `program_roles`, and `audit_findings` collections** and their row types.
   Nothing reads them yet.
3. **Add `sync_tasks`, move `DirectusClient` into `crm`,** and add the queue planner, worker, and
   unit tests.
4. **Move `clubspot-sync` onto the queue.** Delete `sync-log.ts`, drop `sync_runs` /
   `sync_program_runs`, add `offerings.synced_through` and `offerings.quiet_runs`, and rewrite
   `backoff.ts` against the offering row.
5. **Add `DirectoryClient` and `GroupSettingsClient` to `gsuite`,** with mocked-SDK tests.
6. **Create `packages/groups-sync` with the membership pass:** class-group plan functions, the
   add-only executor, and the CLI. Seeds from each program's current offering forward.
7. **Add the settings, nesting, manager, and owner passes.**
8. **Add the audit pass** writing `audit_findings`.
9. **Deploy it:** the `groups-sync` Dockerfile target, the bootstrap identity and its self
   `tokenCreator` grant, the Directus machine user and token, the Cloud Run job and scheduler, and the
   new `docs/manual-setup.md` steps.
10. **Retire the replaced GAM scripts.** Delete `update-groups-from-contacts` and
    `update-groups-from-roles`. Keep `export-groups`, `export-group-members`, `apply-templates`, the
    justfile, and the README as the break-glass path. Update the `gam` README, `docs/crm-schema.md`,
    and CLAUDE.md's package list and dependency graph.

Both answered properly this time.

## #2 — I checked. There's a real finding here.

What I was asking, in plain terms: the job needs permission to write Google Groups. The repo's only proven way to get that is **domain-wide delegation** — the service account impersonates `master@` and acts as them. That works, but it's a manual Admin-console step, and every group change shows up in the audit log as `master@` rather than as the job.

There's a second way I wasn't sure about: assign a Workspace **admin role directly to the service account**, no impersonation. I've now confirmed it:

- **Admin SDK Directory API — confirmed supported.** Google's 2020 announcement explicitly names the Admin SDK Groups API as working with an admin role on a service account, no DWD. This is the API that does membership, which is the bulk of the job.
- **Groups Settings API — not mentioned anywhere.** That's the older API that applies your GAM templates (`allowExternalMembers`, `whoCanPostMessage`). Neither the announcement nor the admin-roles help page covers it, and Google's docs don't say it's excluded either. Genuinely unknown.

So the likely shape is: assign the **Groups Administrator** role to `groups-sync-runner`, get membership with no delegation at all, and find out about settings by trying it. If settings turn out to need DWD, the fallback is clean — the design already keeps `gam/scripts/apply-templates` as break-glass, so settings stay manual in v1 and only membership is automated. The one thing that fallback also costs is the audit's settings-drift check, since reading settings uses the same API.

**Nothing needed from you.** I'll have the design updated to lead with the admin-role path and treat DWD as the fallback. It's strictly better — fewer manual steps, narrower privilege (group access only, not "acts as a super-admin"), and honest audit logs.

## #4 — the three assumptions, concretely

**a) A program gets a group only if someone sets `group_id`.** The sync never guesses. Summer camp weeks, LTS classes, one-off clinics get nothing unless a staff member creates a `groups` row and points the program at it. *If this is wrong*, there's a rule I should encode instead — "every program in category X always gets a group," say. *Risk as written*: you add a new race team next season, forget the group row, and the sync silently does nothing for it. I can have the audit raise "program with no group" so that failure is visible rather than silent — want that?

**b) These groups are for discussion, not the newsletter.** #71 says "keep Groups for discussion, Listmonk for the newsletter," and I've assumed this work doesn't change that — Listmonk later gets its own separate list sync from the same CRM. *If this is wrong*, and `j-pod@` is also what you'd blast a season newsletter to, that changes the settings templates (announcement-only vs. members-can-post) and makes the Listmonk sync partly redundant. Put plainly: **is `j-pod@` parents and coaches talking to each other, or is it a list you send *to*?**

**c) Group owners are a config constant, not CRM data.** `master@` now, `commander@` once #81 lands, as a list in the job's config. Adding an owner means editing config and redeploying, not ticking a box in Directus. *If this is wrong*, owners become a `groups` field or a `program_roles` role. *My reason for config*: group ownership is a break-glass security boundary, and I'd rather it not be editable by anyone with Directus admin-UI access.

Answer (b) and (a)'s follow-up and I'll get the doc updated and committed, then start on step 1.

# Capture an Issue

Turn a problem — from the current conversation or the user's description — into a well-formed GitHub issue in `cyc-seattle/isthmia`.

## When to file one

File an issue when the work will outlive the current session: a problem found mid-task that you
are deliberately not fixing now, a known defect with no owner, or work that needs to be scheduled.

Do **not** file an issue for work you are about to do in this session. The session's pull request
records it. See the Workflow section of `CLAUDE.md`.

## Steps

1. **Gather the problem.** Pull details from the conversation or ask the user. A good issue needs: what's wrong or wanted, where in the code (`path:line`), and why it matters.
2. **Check for duplicates first.** `gh issue list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,labels`. If it overlaps an existing issue, tell the user and offer to comment on / rescope that one instead of filing a new duplicate.
3. **Pick a type label:** `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, or `docker`.
4. **Assign a priority label** using the rubric below.
5. **Write the body** using the template below. Reference concrete files as `path:line`.
6. **Create it:** `gh issue create --title "<imperative title>" --label "<type>,<priority>" --body "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`
7. **Report** the issue number and URL back to the user.

## Priority rubric (P0–P3)

- **P0 — Critical:** data integrity/corruption, production broken, or a security-critical hole. Work starts immediately.
- **P1 — High:** a significant bug or friction the user hits regularly, with no safe workaround (e.g. auth/tooling breakage).
- **P2 — Medium:** a real improvement or a bug with a workaround (added tests, hardening, moderate bugs).
- **P3 — Low:** cleanup, docs, polish, low-risk nice-to-haves.

## Body template

Keep it tight. Use `## Problem` always; then `## Fix` (bugs) or `## Proposed changes` / `## Scope` (enhancements); add `## Impact` when the "why" isn't obvious.

```markdown
## Problem

<what's wrong/wanted, with `path:line` references and a code snippet if useful>

## Fix

<concrete change; mention adding a regression test for bugs>

## Impact

<why it matters — omit if self-evident>
```

## Conventions

- **Title:** short, imperative, no priority prefix (priority lives in the label). e.g. "safeCall retries non-retryable errors with a 60s delay".
- Labels already exist: `P0`–`P3`, `bug`, `enhancement`, `documentation`, `docker`. Don't invent new ones without asking.
- For bugs, always note that the fix should include a regression test — tests live in `packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts`.
- Cross-link related issues with `#N` and note dependencies ("land #47 first").

# Implement a Task

Hand one scoped change to a sub-agent. The sub-agent edits, verifies, and commits. You review the result.

The sub-agent starts cold. It knows nothing about the session, the previous tasks, or the conversation. Everything it needs goes in the brief.

## 1. Prepare the brief

Find the exact `path:line` anchors yourself before you write the brief. A brief that names a file and a line is worth far more than one that describes a symptom.

## 2. Dispatch

Use `Agent` with `subagent_type: implementer`.

The agent already knows the conventions, the test pattern, the `just` rules, and the git rules — they are in `.claude/agents/implementer.md`. Do not repeat them. The brief carries only what is specific to this task:

**Task.** What to change, concretely, with `path:line` anchors.

**Scope fence.** The exact boundary of this change. Name anything adjacent it must not touch.

**Context it cannot derive.** A decision already made, a constraint from the design doc, a reason the obvious approach is wrong. If an approved design doc covers this step, give its path and the step number.

**Never ask for a comment.** Give the agent the constraint and let the standing rule in `CLAUDE.md` decide whether it earns a comment. A brief that says "leave a comment explaining why" overrides that rule, and the agent will write five lines where none were needed.

**Acceptance.** How to know the change worked — the behavior that should differ, or the test that should now pass.

## 3. Review the result

1. Run `git show --stat HEAD`. Read the full diff if the change is non-trivial.
2. Check that the diff stayed inside the scope fence.
3. Summarize for the user in two or three lines: what changed, whether the checks passed, and anything the sub-agent flagged.

If the work is wrong or too wide, dispatch a follow-up sub-agent or run `git revert`. Do not patch it by hand — that defeats the point of delegating.

## Rules

- Dispatch sub-agents in parallel only when their file sets are disjoint. Serialize anything
  touching the same file, the same package, or `packages/crm/schema.yaml`.
- Every agent stages explicit paths, never `-A` or `.` — the git index is shared, and a sweep
  commits another agent's unfinished work.
- One commit per task. A bad task can then be reverted without unpicking the batch.
- If the sub-agent reports the task is bigger than described, stop and move it to `design`.
- If `just check` or `just test` will not pass after two honest attempts, stop and ask the user.

One commit. Stage explicit paths under `packages/crm/` and `packages/clubspot-sync/` only.

persisted state, no retry, and a sandbox that cannot reach Google), and not Cloud Tasks, GCP
Workflows, or Temporal. The driver is failure visibility and blast radius, not latency, so the
queue is a collection you can read and retry in the admin UI. Both syncs move onto it.

relationship between a person and a program, held mostly by people with no Directus login at all

even remove a column — `program_id` still has to live on the join row — while it would add auth
roles that grant nothing and blur the authentication/authorization split `docs/architecture.md`
keeps deliberate. If a volunteer later needs to sign in, they get a Directus role *as well*, which
is the correct relationship between the two.

A Directus role is an **auth** role: it decides what an API caller may read and write, it is global rather than per-program, and it is IaC-managed in `directus-roles.ts`. "Parent Coordinator for Double-handed" is a relationship between a person and a program. Three concrete problems with the FK:

2. Most coordinators have no login at all — `people.directus_user_id` is nullable and usually null. A role pointing at an identity that does not exist is meaningless.

But I think the real objection is the hardcoded enum, and that part is fair. So `role_id` now points at a small staff-maintained `program_role_types` collection — `name` plus a `grants_group_manager` boolean, seeded with the two roles the bash script hardcodes today. Adding a volunteer role becomes data entry rather than a deploy, and `grants_group_manager` puts the group-manager mapping in data instead of in `update-groups-from-roles`.

If your intent was that these volunteers will eventually log in, say so — they would then get a Directus role **as well**, which is the correct relationship between the two, not a replacement for this.

A parent coordinator is a person-program relationship, usually held by someone with no login (`people.directus_user_id` is nullable and mostly null). Adding a volunteer role becomes data entry instead of a deploy, and the group-manager mapping moves out of the bash script into data. **One that needs your decision:**

4. **The job in `packages/crm`** — done, but it breaks a stated rule. `clubspot-sync` depends on `crm`, so once `crm` depends on `gsuite`, clubspot-sync gets Google transitively — and CLAUDE.md says clubspot-sync has "no gsuite dependency, by design". 3: I want to think about this a little more; it's a bit like the groups/google_groups decision, and core to the whole architecture of this thing, which is basically an integration platform for syncing data between various SaaS-tools: Clubspot, Google Workspace, and Directus users for now, eventually other things. ## The shape this fits into

This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the **canonical** model, and each SaaS
product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains:

```text
packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new, this work)
```

The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
SaaS product is named for that product.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the Double-handed
program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google Group" is a
Google Workspace mapping and lives in a `google_`-prefixed collection. The same role later maps to
a Directus policy through its own mapping, without the canonical row changing.

Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
which is why `people.directus_user_id` is already a provider-specific column on a canonical table.

input.content:
Reframed the whole doc around the integration-platform framing. `b6eb90f9`.

There is a new section at the top, **The shape this fits into**, stating the rule so it outlives this work: *a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one SaaS product is named for that product.* Step 10 now copies that rule into CLAUDE.md.

**On 4 — `packages/gsuite-sync`, not inside `crm`.** Google Workspace's side of the platform, mirroring `clubspot-sync` on Clubspot's. Groups today; Workspace users or shared drives later go here rather than in a third package. Worth noting this dissolves the dependency problem on its own — `crm` goes back to being schema-and-types with no jobs and no `gsuite` dependency, so nothing reaches `clubspot-sync` transitively. The "no gsuite dependency, by design" note still gets dropped in step 10, since the boundary that matters is one provider per sync package, not a transitive import.

**On 3 — the canonical/provider split, applied.** `program_role_types` is now canonical and carries *only* a name. "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of Double-handed" is the whole of what it says. The Google behaviour moved out to `google_group_roles` (`program_role_type_id` → `MEMBER`/`MANAGER`/`OWNER`), which is the mapping `update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today. A Directus-policy mapping later is the same pattern with a different provider.

Two consequences I applied for consistency, both worth a look since they go further than your comment:

1. **The group→canonical FK reversed direction.** `google_groups` now carries nullable `program_id` and `class_id` instead of `programs.google_group_id`. Otherwise every canonical table grows a column per SaaS product. Staff still see the group on a program's detail page via an O2M alias, the same trick `my_contacts` uses.
2. **Three schemas instead of one**, each owned by the package that owns the concern: `crm` canonical, `directus` infrastructure (`sync_tasks` + `audit_findings`), `gsuite-sync` provider. `audit_findings` moved to infrastructure and got a `source` column, because `unlinked_offering` is a Clubspot finding, not a Google one.

**The question I could not settle for you** is now open question 1: the principle applied strictly also condemns `offerings.clubspot_camp_id`, `sessions.clubspot_session_id`, and `people.directus_user_id` — provider columns on canonical tables, all pre-existing.

My recommendation is to draw the line at **structure and behaviour, not identity**. An external id is provenance: the row would not exist without it, and hoisting it into a side table costs a join on every upsert in the sync hot path for no behavioural gain. Provider structure (the group graph) and provider behaviour (which Google role a volunteer gets) do earn their own collections. If you want the strict version it is a separate piece of work across every sync, not something to fold in here.

Pushed `b6eb90f9` with a summary comment on the PR.

**The framing is now a section at the top of the doc**, so it outlives this work, and step 10 copies it into CLAUDE.md:

```
packages/directus      infrastructure — the REST client and the durable queue
packages/crm           the canonical domain: schema.yaml and its row types. No jobs.
packages/clubspot-sync Clubspot         <-> crm
packages/gsuite-sync   Google Workspace <-> crm     (new)
```

**On 4** — `packages/gsuite-sync`. Worth noting it dissolves the dependency question on its own: `crm` goes back to schema-and-types with no jobs and no `gsuite`, so nothing reaches `clubspot-sync` transitively. The CLAUDE.md note still gets dropped, since the boundary that matters is one provider per sync package.

**On 3** — `program_role_types` is canonical and carries only a name. Google behaviour moved to `google_group_roles` (`program_role_type_id` → `MEMBER`/`MANAGER`/`OWNER`), which is exactly the mapping `update-groups-from-roles:38-51` hardcodes today. A Directus-policy mapping later is the same pattern, different provider.

**Two things I took further than you asked**, because the principle seemed to demand it — push back if I overreached:

1. **The group FK reversed.** `google_groups` carries nullable `program_id`/`class_id`, rather than `programs.google_group_id`. Otherwise every canonical table grows a column per SaaS product. The Directus UI still shows the group on a program via an O2M alias, same as `my_contacts`.
2. **Three schemas, not one** — `crm` canonical, `directus` infrastructure, `gsuite-sync` provider. `audit_findings` moved to infrastructure with a `source` column, since `unlinked_offering` is a Clubspot finding and not a Google one.

**What I couldn't settle for you** is now open question 1. Applied strictly, the principle also condemns `offerings.clubspot_camp_id`, `sessions.clubspot_session_id`, and `people.directus_user_id` — all pre-existing provider columns on canonical tables. My recommendation is to draw the line at **structure and behaviour, not identity**: an external id is provenance, the row wouldn't exist without it, and hoisting it into a side table costs a join on every upsert in the sync hot path for no behavioural gain. If you want the strict version, that's separate work across every sync.

Implementation still paused; the worktree is back on `session/groups-sync` with the WIP commit intact.

I think #2 makes a lot of sense: decoupling the schema by app/provider/domain is clean. I'm not so sure about #1 - if it applies to gsuite, it should apply to other providers.  I think the FK being on the canonical entity is fine: maybe the solution is to allow providers to "extend" the core schemas?

That's better than my reversal — it keeps the FK where it reads naturally while ownership stays explicit, and it makes Clubspot consistent instead of grandfathered. Whether it's cheap depends entirely on whether the schema-apply machinery can handle a package owning *fields* on a collection it doesn't own. Let me check.

The rule that follows: **a canonical collection describes the org, and anything specific to one
SaaS product is owned by that product's package.** "Fred is a Parent Coordinator of the
Double-handed program" is canonical. "A Parent Coordinator is a manager of that program's Google
Group" is a Google Workspace mapping. The same role later maps to a Directus policy through its
own mapping, without the canonical row changing.

Directus is both the canonical store and a provider in its own right — it has users and roles —
which is why `people.directus_user_id` is a provider-specific column on a canonical table.

### Providers extend canonical collections

Ownership is about **which schema declares a thing**, not about which table it sits on. A provider
may add a field to a canonical collection: `programs.google_group_id` is a real column on
`programs`, declared in `gsuite-sync`'s schema, not in `crm`'s. Staff see it where they expect it,
and the canonical package still knows nothing about Google.

The machinery for this already half exists. `scopeSnapshot`
(`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:341-349`) is what makes "my schema does not
mention collection X" mean "leave X alone" rather than "delete X" (#109). It is
**collection-granular** today: `owned` is a set of collection names and every live entry under
them is replaced. It needs to become field-granular — `owned` splits into collections this package
owns outright and `collection.field` pairs it owns on someone else's collection, with `fields` and
`relations` filtered on both. The comment at `client.ts:297-298` asserts the owning side of a
relation is always a collection this app owns; extension fields break that and it needs rewording.

Consequences, all mild:

- Provider schemas apply **after** the canonical one, since the collection must exist first. The
  justfile already orders projects.
- `just directus-local` must apply every package's schema, not only `packages/crm/schema.yaml`.
- Permission rules are collection-level, so a provider's field on `programs` is already covered by
  the existing `programs` rules. Nothing to add.
- Row types do not compose automatically: `ProgramRow` in `crm` will not carry `google_group_id`.
  Consumers that need both intersect the two types.

Implements `.claude/plans/crm-to-google-groups-sync.md`, approved in the review threads above. Tracked by #143, carved out of #71.

## What this does

Group membership is maintained by hand today — `gam/scripts/update-groups-from-contacts` hardcodes six `camp|class|group` mappings that get edited every season. This makes it a consequence of CRM data instead.

Three things land together, because the sync needs all of them:

1. **`programs` splits into durable `programs` + dated `offerings`.** A Clubspot Camp is an *instance* of a program. Breaking change; all CRM data re-syncs.
2. **A durable task queue** (`sync_tasks`) in a new `packages/directus`, with per-item retry and a backlog visible in the admin UI. Both syncs move onto it.
3. **`packages/gsuite-sync`**, a Cloud Run job that writes Google Groups from the CRM, add-only, with an audit pass that reports rather than removes.

## The framing it establishes

This repo is an integration platform. Directus holds the canonical model; each SaaS product gets a sync package that maps it to one or more app domains. Anything specific to one product is owned by that product's package — including fields it adds to canonical collections, which is what makes `programs.google_group_id` a `gsuite-sync` field on a `crm` collection. Step 12 records the rule in CLAUDE.md, since it outlives this work.

## Steps

- [ ] 1. Split `programs` into `programs` + `offerings`
- [ ] 2. Canonical `program_role_types` and `program_roles`
- [ ] 3. Make `scopeSnapshot` field-granular so providers can extend canonical collections
- [ ] 4. `packages/directus`: `DirectusClient`, `sync_tasks`, `audit_findings`, queue and worker
- [ ] 5. Move `clubspot-sync` onto the queue
- [ ] 6. `DirectoryClient` and `GroupSettingsClient` in `gsuite`
- [ ] 7. `packages/gsuite-sync` with the membership pass
- [ ] 8. Settings, nesting, manager and owner passes
- [ ] 9. The audit pass
- [ ] 10. Deploy: image, identity, machine user, job and scheduler
- [ ] 11. Move existing provider id columns to their owners' schemas
- [ ] 12. Retire the replaced GAM scripts; update CLAUDE.md and docs

## Open

Whether the Groups Settings API accepts a service-account role assignment rather than domain-wide delegation. Gates step 8 only; the fallback is leaving settings with `gam/scripts/apply-templates`, which step 12 keeps.

Step 1 of the approved design at `.claude/plans/crm-to-google-groups-sync.md`. Read that doc's "Schema" section first; this brief does not repeat it. You are on branch `plan/groups-sync`.

## Task

Today `programs` is one row per Clubspot Camp, keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. That is wrong: a Camp is a *dated instance* of a program. "2026 Fall Double-handed Race Team" and "2026 Spring Double-handed Race Team" are two Camps of one program, "Double-handed Race Team". Split the level in two.

**`packages/crm/schema.yaml`:**

- New collection `offerings` — `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, and a **nullable** `program_id` FK to `programs`. This is the Clubspot-Camp-level row.
- `programs` (collection block at `schema.yaml:224`) keeps `id` and `name`, **loses `clubspot_camp_id`**, and becomes the durable catalog entry — created and named by staff, never by the sync. Leave `category` alone.
- Repoint these FKs from `program_id` to `offering_id`, pointing at `offerings`: `sessions` (`:387`), `classes` (`:5`), `registrations` (`:335`), `custom_field_definitions` (`:59`).
- `sync_program_runs.program_id` (`:413`, and `packages/crm/src/sync-log.ts:22-23`) points at the Camp-level row, so it becomes `offering_id` -> `offerings`. Keep it nullable for the reason its note already gives.
- Give `offerings` an icon and note matching its neighbours' style, and fix the `programs` note — it currently says "A program is Clubspot's Camp", which is now exactly backwards.

**`packages/crm/src/`:**

- `schedule.ts:5-10` — `ProgramRow` loses `clubspot_camp_id`; add `OfferingRow` with `clubspot_camp_id`, `name`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `program_id: string | null`. Update the header comment at `schedule.ts:2`.
- `schedule.ts:13`, `:23` — `SessionRow.program_id` and `ClassRow.program_id` become `offering_id`.
- `registrations.ts:8`, `:52` and `sync-log.ts:23` — same rename.

**`packages/clubspot-sync/src/`:**

- `schedule.ts:91` — `planPrograms` becomes `planOfferings`, returning `CollectionPlan<OfferingRow>`, still keyed on `clubspot_camp_id`. **It must never write `program_id`** — not on create, not on update. Staff set that link by hand and a nightly re-sync must not undo it. This is the single most important behavioural constraint in this step.
- `schedule.ts:14` — `SCHEDULE_CREATE_ORDER` leads with `offerings`.
- `schedule.ts:107`, `:134` — the `requireLookup` calls and the `programCrmIdByClubspotCampId` map rename to offering equivalents.
- `registrations.ts:98`, `:327` and `sync-run.ts:10, 26, 119, 133, 144, 156, 260, 272-277, 545, 568, 588` — carry the rename through.
- Tests: `test/schedule.test.ts`, `test/sync-run.test.ts`, `test/sync-log-writer.test.ts`, `test/promoted-fields.test.ts`, `test/registrations.test.ts`.

Add a unit test asserting `planOfferings` leaves an existing row's `program_id` untouched when Clubspot reports a change to that camp. That is the regression this step exists to prevent.

## Scope fence

One commit. Stage explicit paths under `packages/crm/` and `packages/clubspot-sync/` only — two other agents are working in `packages/infrastructure/` and `packages/gsuite/` at the same time and the git index is shared.

Do **not**:

- Add `program_roles`, `program_role_types`, `google_groups`, `google_group_roles`, `audit_findings`, or `sync_tasks` — later steps.
- Add `programs.google_group_id` — that is a `gsuite-sync` extension field in step 7.
- Touch `backoff.ts`, delete `sync-log.ts`, or add `offerings.synced_through` / `offerings.quiet_runs` — step 5.
- Touch `packages/infrastructure/`, `packages/gsuite/`, `gam/`, `docs/`, `CLAUDE.md`, or the justfile.

The one exception: if the build or an existing test fails without an `offerings` entry in the permission lists at `packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:107-121`, make that minimal change and say so in your report.

## Context you cannot derive

- **Breaking changes are approved.** No manual Directus edits exist and all data re-syncs from Clubspot. Do not write a migration, a compatibility shim, or a deprecated alias.
- **The sync never creates a program.** Clubspot has no durable program identity. `offerings.program_id` stays null until a staff member sets it in the Directus UI. An offering with no program is a normal state — do not throw, do not warn per row.
- The repo rule that an unresolvable reference is skipped with a warning while a missing required value throws still holds, but a null `program_id` is neither: it is expected.

## Acceptance

- `just check` and `just test` pass.
- `just directus-local` applies the schema cleanly to a fresh instance — run it, it is the only real check that the YAML is valid and the relations resolve. Tear down with `just directus-local-down` after.
- The new test proves `planOfferings` never emits `program_id`.
- `grep -rn "program_id" packages/crm/src packages/clubspot-sync/src` returns only `offerings.program_id` itself; every other occurrence has become `offering_id`.

Step 3 of the approved design at `.claude/plans/crm-to-google-groups-sync.md`. Read its "Providers extend canonical collections" section first; this brief does not repeat the reasoning. You are on branch `plan/groups-sync`.

## Task

Make a package able to own **fields** on a collection it does not own, so a provider package can add a column to a canonical collection. Nothing uses this yet — it is the enabling step, proved on its own so a later step is not debugging two new things at once.

**`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts`:**

- `scopeSnapshot` (`:341-349`) is collection-granular: `owned` is a `Set<string>` of collection names, and `keepLive` drops every live `collections`/`fields`/`relations` entry whose `collection` is in that set, replacing them with the app schema's entries. Make it field-granular:
  - Collections a package owns outright — from `appSchema.collections` — keep today's behaviour.
  - Fields the package owns on a collection it does *not* own — every `appSchema.fields` entry whose collection is not owned outright — are identified by `collection` + `field`. A live `fields` entry is dropped only when its collection is owned outright **or** its `collection.field` pair is owned. Same rule for `relations`, which are also keyed by `collection` + `field`.
  - The result: a provider schema declaring only `programs.google_group_id` leaves every other `programs` field exactly as it lives today, and a field that package removes from its schema does get dropped.
- `DirectusSnapshotEntry` (`:299-301`) needs an optional `field`.
- `collectionsInSchema` (`:323-325`) — decide whether it stays as-is or gains a sibling. Its one caller (`packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:45`) uses it to generate per-collection Staff permission rules, and extension fields need no new permission rules, so it should keep returning only wholly-owned collections. Confirm that against the code rather than taking my word for it.
- The comment at `:297-298` asserts a relation's owning side is always a collection this app owns. Extension fields break that. Reword it.
- Check `hasCollectionDelete` (`:365-370`) still behaves for a schema that declares fields but no collections.

**`justfile` / `scripts/directus-local`:** the script hardcodes `../crm/schema.yaml` (`scripts/directus-local:64`) and derives `expected_collections` from it (`:69`). Teach it to apply every package's schema in order, canonical first, so a local instance is complete. Today `packages/crm/schema.yaml` is the only one, so make the list easy to extend rather than inventing files that do not exist yet.

**Tests** go in `packages/infrastructure/test/directus-client.test.ts` (537 lines, `describe("applySchema")` at `:54`, `describe("collectionsInSchema")` at `:48`). Cover at least: a provider schema adding one field to a collection it does not own leaves that collection's other fields untouched; removing that field from the provider schema drops it; and a collection owned outright still gets replaced wholesale.

## Scope fence

One commit. Stage explicit paths under `packages/infrastructure/` plus `justfile` and `scripts/directus-local` only — two other agents are working in `packages/crm/` + `packages/clubspot-sync/` and in `packages/gsuite/` at the same time, and the git index is shared. Do not touch those packages, `gam/`, `docs/`, or `CLAUDE.md`.

Do not add any new collection or field to any schema. This step changes the apply *mechanism* only.

## Context you cannot derive

- `scopeSnapshot` exists because `/schema/diff` has no notion of ownership — it diffs the entire instance against whatever you hand it, so an app's snapshot omitting a collection reads as "delete it". Scoping to "exactly what this app owns, plus everything else as it lives today" is the whole fix (#109). Your change extends that from collections to fields without weakening it: a field nobody declares must still be left alone, never deleted.
- Apply order is guaranteed by the justfile running projects in sequence, not by anything in the code. A provider schema is applied after the canonical one so the collection already exists. You do not need to enforce that in `scopeSnapshot`.

## Acceptance

- `just check` and `just test` pass.
- `just directus-local` still applies cleanly to a fresh instance; tear down with `just directus-local-down` after.
- The new tests fail against the current collection-granular implementation and pass against yours. Say in your report that you verified this, or why you could not.

Step 6 of the approved design at `.claude/plans/crm-to-google-groups-sync.md`. You are on branch `plan/groups-sync`. Nothing consumes this yet — a later step builds the sync job on it.

## Task

Add Google Admin SDK clients to `packages/gsuite`, alongside the existing `CalendarClient` and `SpreadsheetClient`.

**New `packages/gsuite/src/directory.ts`:**

- `DirectoryClient` — Admin SDK Directory API, groups and members. It needs enough to: get a group, create a group, list a group's members, add a member with a role (`MEMBER` / `MANAGER` / `OWNER`), and update an existing member's role. Adding a group as a member of another group goes through the same members endpoint with the sub-group's address, so it needs no separate method.
- `GroupSettingsClient` — Groups Settings API: read a group's settings, and patch them from a settings object.

Both take an `Auth.GoogleAuth` in the constructor, exactly as `CalendarClient` does (`packages/gsuite/src/calendar.ts:26-28`). Impersonation and scopes are the caller's problem, not the client's — do not construct auth inside these classes.

Wrap every API call in `safeCall` (`packages/gsuite/src/common.ts:85`), like the existing clients, so rate limiting and the retry policy apply.

Export both from `packages/gsuite/src/index.ts` (currently three `export *` lines).

**Tests** in `packages/gsuite/test/directory.test.ts`, mocking the `googleapis` boundary. `packages/gsuite/test/calendar.test.ts` is the closest existing pattern — follow it. Cover the member-role paths in particular, since those are what the sync depends on.

## Scope fence

One commit. Stage explicit paths under `packages/gsuite/` only — two other agents are working in `packages/crm/` + `packages/clubspot-sync/` and in `packages/infrastructure/` at the same time, and the git index is shared.

Do not create `packages/gsuite-sync`, touch any Directus schema, add anything to `packages/infrastructure`, or edit `gam/`, `docs/`, or `CLAUDE.md`.

`packages/gsuite` already depends on `googleapis` — no new dependency should be needed. If you believe one is, stop and say so rather than adding it.

## Context you cannot derive

- **A group member can be an arbitrary external email address**, not just a Workspace account. Guardians are on personal Gmail. Do not validate or restrict the member address domain.
- **Membership writes must be able to distinguish "already a member" from a real failure.** The sync is add-only and idempotent, so adding someone who is already in the group is the common case, not an error. Google returns 409 for a duplicate member. Decide how the client surfaces that — a typed result or a documented throw the caller can catch — and make it explicit in the signature rather than leaving the caller to parse a status code.
- `safeCall` already treats 429 and 5xx as retryable and everything else as a hard failure (`packages/gsuite/src/common.ts:51-60`). A 409 must not be retried.

## Acceptance

- `just check` and `just test` pass.
- No live Google API call in any test.

**Step 6 done** — `6f1f254b`, 482 lines across three files, all inside `packages/gsuite/`. Scope clean, `just check` and `just test` pass.

What I verified rather than took on trust:

- **The duplicate-member path is right.** `addMember` returns `"added" | "already-member"` and catches 409 rather than throwing; anything else still throws. This matters because the sync is add-only and idempotent, so "already a member" is the *common* case, not an error. And `safeCall` only retries 429/5xx, so a 409 won't get retried into a delay loop.
- **The `as any` on the auth cast** matches `CalendarClient` exactly (`calendar.ts:29`) — existing precedent, not a new shortcut.

The agent hit a genuine repo-specific type-inference problem worth knowing about: with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` plus `preserveSymlinks`, passing an explicitly-`undefined` optional into a `Schema$X` field silently resolves to the wrong `googleapis` overload and types as `void`. It worked around it by giving `safeCall` its generic explicitly and building request bodies conditionally — the same shape `spreadsheet.ts` already uses, so no new idiom.

**Filed #145** for the pre-existing `calendar.ts` gap — it has no `safeCall` at all, so Calendar requests get no rate limiting or retry, and a transient 429 fails the whole `calendar-sync` run. Left out of the diff per the convention.
